killedBy: startGameWith: level progression advances one level on an intermediate win, carrying the surviving lives
one run, from Launch to the next mission (issue #323) carries one campaign run through every phase without losing its place
why: Drops the lives argument, so `switchTo` falls back to a full pool and every mission boundary silently refills the run -- a campaign that cannot be lost. Two tests catch it and they catch it differently, which is the point of naming both: the first drives the win directly and reads the next board's lives; the second is issue #323's chained scenario, where the life was spent by a REAL death several hops earlier and has to survive a pause, a resume, an ending and a navigation to be missing here. Neither is redundant -- one pins the arithmetic at the boundary, the other pins that the run is the same run across the whole sequence.
